attributes.morphology: typical dendritic structure with interdendritic and dendritic regions

evidence.quote: All four alloys exhibit typical dendritic structures, likely due to the slow solidification process. The grey regions correspond to inter-dendritic (ID) areas, whereas the bright white regions represent dendritic regions (DRs).
As shown in Fig. 3 (e), the ID regions of Nb0.33 exhibit complex precipitates, with a significant presence of submicron-sized secondary phase particles with an average size of 0.79 μm.

Although no secondary phase diffraction peaks were observed in the XRD patterns for Nb0.75, a small number of complex precipitates were detected in the ID regions, as shown in Fig. 3 (f). This observation indicates that as the Nb concentration increases, the amount of grain boundary precipitates decreases.
the BCC-dendritic structure within and along the edges of the shear band is elongated in the direction of shear band propagation
The average width of the shear band is 14.59 μ m, and the BCC-dendritic structure within and along the edges of the shear band is elongated in the direction of shear band propagation.
Small, shallow intergranular dimples were also observed.

A small amount of the Laves phase precipitated interdendritically in ZrV, indicating that during dynamic compression, cracks preferentially nucleate at the Laves phase and subsequently propagate along grain boundaries.

Nb0.75 achieved 2062 MPa for a strain rate of 3012 s 1, an increase of 13.9 % compared to the average yield strength of TiZrNbV for the same strain rate [17].

Among the four alloys, Nb0.75 exhibits the lowest critical velocity for impact-induced reactions (17.56 m/s), which is attributed to the cleavage fracture triggered by dislocation pile-up and thermal softening effects.
